card.title: GPS clocks need a relativity fix

body.claim: Special and general relativity predicted that the clocks on GPS satellites, as observed by those on Earth, run 38 microseconds faster per day than those on the Earth.
body.why: The design of GPS corrects for this difference. It makes two corrections to its time signals: one for relative velocity of satellite and receiver, using the special theory of relativity, and one for the difference in gravitational potential, using general relativity.

probes.question: How much faster per day do GPS satellite clocks run than clocks on Earth, as predicted by relativity?
True or false: GPS's design corrects for the difference in clock speed that relativity predicts.
